items.title: Road to clean skies: assessing the effects of low-carbon transport systems policy on monthly air pollution
items.authors: Jiali He, Jinxing Guo, Jingyi Meng, Lei Jiang
items.summary: The transportation sector is a major source of urban air pollution. Using county-level monthly panel data from China for 2007–2019, this paper evaluates two rounds of the low-carbon transport systems pilot policy introduced in 2011 and 2012 through a staggered difference-in-differences design. The fully controlled baseline specification indicates an approximately 2.1% reduction in monthly PM2.5 concentrations, statistically significant at the 5% level. Mechanism analyses provide evidence consistent with cleaner and more efficient energy use, changes in transportation structure, and expanded public transit as potential channels. items.title: Research on the Coordinated Development of Urban Green Infrastructure Construction and Carbon Neutrality
items.summary: This study systematically explores the intrinsic mechanism and implementation path of the coordinated development of urban green infrastructure (UGI) and carbon neutrality. Based on the four-dimensional analysis framework of input carbon effect synergy institutional guarantee, the contribution characteristics of UGI to carbon neutrality were revealed through remote sensing inversion, model simulation, and multiple case comparisons. items.title: Advancements in Pipeline Corrosion Monitoring for Supercritical CO2 Environments: A Review
items.authors: Prosper Dadzie, Aliyu Adebayo Sulaimon, Shiferaw Regassa Jufar, Yen Adams Sokama‐Neuyam, Joshua Nsiah Turkson, Muhammad Ayoub et al.
items.summary: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) technology ensures that captured CO2 is compressed and transported through pipelines in its supercritical state (SC-CO2) to allow for large-scale storage and utilization. SC-CO2 corrosion is a difficult challenge to pipeline transportation due to the extremely high-temperature-pressure conditions and impurities such as water, SO2, O2, H2S, and NO2. Review articles on the subject have mostly focused on the mechanism, factors contributing to the corrosion, and prevention/control strategies, with limited attention paid to monitoring techniques. This study aimed to review the extant literature on corrosion evaluation and monitoring, to supplement…

items.title: Balancing CO2 Mass Transport and Salt Precipitation via Multiparameter Optimization for Efficient Syngas Production in MEA Electrolyzers
items.authors: Pan Huang, Shaojie Zheng, Xuefeng He, Hao Lei, Zhenting Xie, Qin Peng et al.
items.summary: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) offers a sustainable route for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals and fuels, yet its practical application is hindered by CO2 transport limitations and salt precipitation in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzers. In this work, we systematically investigated the effects of catalyst loading, gas diffusion layer (GDL) wettability, CO2 flow rate, CO2 temperature, and acid-vapor humidification on the eCO2RR performance.
